# Am I Cooked

> Am I Cooked is a free, open-source (MIT) MCP server that runs on a student's laptop and connects Claude Desktop, Claude Code or ChatGPT to their D2L Brightspace courses: grades, assignments and due dates, announcements, course content and files. Every tool is read-only. Not affiliated with or endorsed by D2L or any university.

The student signs in on their school's own login page in a real browser window. Am I Cooked keeps the session in `~/.amicooked` on the laptop and never sees the password. Downloaded files go to `~/Downloads/amicooked`. Setup has presets for McMaster, Waterloo, Western, Queen's, Guelph, Laurier, TMU, uOttawa, Carleton, Brock, Windsor, Laurentian and Lakehead, and accepts any Brightspace URL. Login is tested at McMaster.

## Setting it up

- [SKILL.md](https://amicooked-mcp.vercel.app/SKILL.md): setup instructions written for AI agents. Start here if a user asks you to set up Am I Cooked. Ask which school they go to; never ask for their password.
- macOS and Linux: `curl -fsSL https://amicooked-mcp.vercel.app/install.sh | sh`
- Windows (PowerShell): `irm https://amicooked-mcp.vercel.app/install.ps1 | iex`
- With Node.js 22 or newer: `npx -y amicooked@0 setup`
- ChatGPT: `amicooked setup --clients chatgpt`, then add the address in ChatGPT under Settings, Apps & Connectors (Developer mode), and enter the pairing code (`amicooked pair` makes a new one). Works while the laptop is on and awake.
- Uninstall: `amicooked uninstall` (`--purge` also deletes login and settings)

## Tools

- `am_i_cooked`: every current course at once (grade so far, what's due, overdue work, new announcements) plus a heat score from 0 to 10 labelled raw, warming up, toasty, cooked or well done
- `get_my_courses`: the student's courses
- `get_my_grades`: grade items and feedback for a course
- `get_upcoming_due_dates`: calendar deadlines, for one course or all
- `get_announcements`: instructor announcements
- `get_assignments`: assignments with due dates and submission status
- `get_course_content`: modules, lectures and files
- `download_file`: save a course file and read its text (PDF, Word, PowerPoint)
- `read_file`: read a file that was already downloaded
